author: a. m. bolton
title: Lindsey Graham announces budget action and supports diplomatic efforts with Iran - Greenville Leader
text:
Senator Lindsey Graham, chairman of the Senate Budget Committee and U.S. Senator representing South Carolina, posted a series of updates on March 25, 2026, addressing legislative actions and foreign policy positions.
In his first post at 12:23 UTC, Graham announced progress on budgetary matters: “After consulting with @POTUS and his team and @LeaderJohnThune, the Senate @BudgetGOP Committee will expeditiously move toward creating a second budget reconciliation bill. The number one priority of the federal government has always been keeping our homeland safe and keeping”.
Later that day at 14:46 UTC, Graham shared his involvement in a judicial nomination hearing: “In just a few minutes, I’ll be introducing Sheria Clarke at her nomination hearing before the @SenJudiciaryGOP Committee. In choosing Sheria to be a federal district court judge, @POTUS has done an outstanding job for the people of South Carolina. LIVE: https://t.co/joBGDmVyQt”.
At 16:03 UTC, Graham commented on ongoing diplomatic efforts regarding Iran: “Not only do I support @POTUS and his team’s efforts to negotiate with Iran to find a solution to the threats this regime presents to the region and the world, I encourage it. It is the outcome I seek, not the method. I have confidence in President Trump’s negotiating team to”.
Lindsey Graham has chaired the Senate Budget Committee and serves on several key committees including Appropriations, Judiciary, and Environment and Public Works (official website). His background includes more than three decades in the U.S. Air Force Reserves where he retired as a colonel. A native of Central, South Carolina who grew up in a blue-collar family that operated a local restaurant and pool hall (official website), Graham’s career has focused on fiscal responsibility and national security priorities.
